PullRequest.Title: ci: run the Linux Electron smoke tests in four shards with measured suite durations
PullRequest.Body:
Runs the Linux Electron smoke tests in Code OSS PR CI in **four** shards instead of three, and rebalances them from measured suite durations. This follows lszomoru's suggestion. Windows and macOS are unchanged.

## Why

Over 30 clean first-attempt PR runs from Nov 8–9, the three Linux shards' jobs took 4.98, **5.53** and 4.99 min (p50). Their test time was 207.5, 246.5 and 222.5 s, plus about 85 s of setup per job. The balancer in `test/smoke/src/shard.ts` used estimates that no longer match:
- `Data Loss (insiders -> insiders)` was 100 s and takes 105 s at p50 (one run was 134 s). `Agents Window (SSH Dev Container AgentHost)` was 50 s and takes 58 s.
- `Data Loss (stable -> insiders)` has runnable tests, so it counted as 20 s, but in PR CI it skips itself without a stable build and takes 0 s.
- Unlisted suites counted as 20 s, while the unlisted Linux suites take 8–12 s.

## Change

- `shard.ts`: Linux gets its own duration table, built from the p50 of each suite over those 30 runs (rounded to 5 s, with `Data Loss (stable -> insiders)` at 0), and a 10 s default. Windows and macOS keep the previous table and the 20 s default, so their shards are assigned exactly as before.
- `pr-linux-test.yml`: adds `electron-smoke-4` and sets all four Linux jobs to `SMOKE_SHARD_TOTAL: '4'`, named `Electron-Smoke (shard N/4)`. Windows stays at three shards in `pr-win32-test.yml`, which is a separate workflow with its own jobs, so nothing is shared to separate.
- `build/lib/test/detectChanges.test.ts` and the smoke tests skill are updated for the new job names.

**Required checks:** `main` requires `PR Gate`, `Dependencies Check`, `license/cla`, `VS Code PR Check` and `Screenshots & Tests`, not the shard job names. `PR Gate` depends on the `linux-tests` caller job, which covers every job of `pr-linux-test.yml`, including the new shard. So no required check waits on a removed name.

## Split (seconds of test time)

| Shard | Today, 3 shards (p50 of 30 runs) | This PR, predicted from those medians | This PR, measured (p50 of 3 runs) | Job time today | Job time with this PR (p50 of 3) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 207.5 | 164 | 181 | 4.98 min | 4.45 min |
| 2 | **246.5** | 166.5 | 143 | **5.53 min** | 3.63 min |
| 3 | 222.5 | 166 | 175 | 4.99 min | 4.47 min |
| 4 | – | 171 | **191** | – | **4.63 min** |

The slowest Linux smoke job goes from **5.53 to 4.63 min (p50)**, or −54 s, for one more 8-core runner per PR.

**Every suite ran exactly once** in each of the 3 runs ([42713185482](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/42713185482), attempts 1–3): the 27 suites with tests, none duplicated, and none missing compared with the 30 baseline runs. Each shard's `smoke-test-runner.log` lists its suites (`Running smoke test shard N/4 with … of 33 suites`), and the 33 cover every registered suite once.

**Why measured differs from predicted:** shards 1, 3 and 4 run slower than the 3-shard medians, and shard 2 faster. That's not one stale estimate:
- `Data Loss (insiders -> insiders)` alone varied from 89 to 127 s across the 3 runs.
- In shard 4, every suite ran 1.5–6 s over its median on all 3 runs. `Language Features` and `Quick Open`, the first suites of shards 4 and 3, ran 6–7 s over, which is the first app launch of a shard.
- In shard 2, the Agents Window suites ran 5–10 s under (`Dev Container` 53–61 s against 70).

Tuning the table further would chase run-to-run and placement effects that a single static table can't capture. Each shard has one first suite, so the cold-start cost is the same for all of them.

**Note:** CI placed some of the 10 s suites differently from my local simulation (for example `Launch` and `Multiroot`). Both splits predict 164–171 s per shard, so the balance is the same.

## Validation

- eslint is clean. `detectChanges.test.ts` passes apart from one test that fails the same way on `main` locally (it depends on the local git setup).
- PR CI is green on all 3 runs. Copilot recommends approval with no open issues.

> Authored with Copilot

Scenarios.Scenario: Product-affecting PR runs Linux Electron smoke tests on the normal warm workspace-image/cache path
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Detect Changes enables electron_smoke_affected; the reusable Linux workflow starts all smoke jobs, each completes shared setup and its assigned smoke suites, the linux-tests caller waits for every job, and PR Gate waits for linux-tests. The slowest of the four shards is therefore on the required-check critical path. The PR reports this falls from 5.53 minutes with three shards to 4.63 minutes with four.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch workspace-image scripts, restore the workspace image and caches, check out Git/LFS content, and restore cached packages/dependencies.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Four concurrent copies per affected PR after the diff, versus three before. On the warm path each job still independently performs cache/image lookups and checkout; the fourth job adds one bounded copy.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same network boundaries ran in each of three smoke jobs. The diff increases their cardinality from three to four but does not add a new boundary type or serialize it.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Each shard must finish its own setup before its smoke subset runs; setup is on each job's critical path, while parallel execution means PR Gate observes only the slowest job rather than the sum.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Install/update dependencies, transpile the client and extensions, prepare Electron, compile smoke/Copilot code, run diagnostics, and launch the Electron smoke runner.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Four setup/compile/runner invocations versus three before. The actual 33 top-level suites remain assigned exactly once in total; only per-job setup grows by one copy.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Three jobs duplicated setup and partitioned the same suite collection into three subsets. The diff changes the bounded job count to four.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Setup and each shard's selected suites are on that shard's path. Rebalancing reduces the longest measured path despite the extra setup copy running in parallel.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Clone the vscode-smoketest-express repository for each isolated runner.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One clone per shard: four concurrent clones after the diff versus three before; retries are per job, up to five only on failure.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Three independent shard jobs each cloned the repository; the fourth job adds one clone.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The clone is in the root before hook and must finish before any selected suite can run. It remains parallel across shards.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Mount/update the workspace image, install/cache files, copy smoke fixtures, write traces/logs, and clean each job's temporary workspace.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Four isolated runner filesystems versus three; work is bounded by the fixed shard count and job-local data.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same job-local filesystem work occurred in three jobs.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Most preparation is before smoke execution; cleanup and final artifact handling can delay individual job completion.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Upload crash data on failure and upload logs after each job.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Normal success uploads one log artifact per shard, now four versus three. Failure-only uploads likewise gain at most one shard's artifacts.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Three shard-specific log artifacts were uploaded.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Log upload occurs before each job completes and can affect the slowest job, but is bounded and parallel.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Fixed Linux shard count (3 to 4), 33 registered top-level suites with 27 runnable in the measured PR environment, and one shared setup sequence per shard. Suite execution cardinality remains one assignment per suite.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Four independent 8-core jobs now run concurrently instead of three. Within each job, the shard selector assigns a disjoint subset of the 33 registered suites; Mocha runs that subset without diff-introduced intra-job parallelism. There is no shared limiter across jobs, but runner selection is explicitly justified as plentiful and the burst is bounded at four.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Workspace images, pnpm store, apt packages, built-in extensions, and Electron are reused when warm; each of four jobs performs its own restore/lookups. A cache miss falls back to downloads/installations independently in each job. There is no cross-job request coalescing, but the increase is a fixed one-job increment rather than input-scaled fan-out.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that shared setup boundaries increase from three to four and that suite execution remains deduplicated; low confidence that the bounded aggregate-resource increase causes any adverse performance symptom.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The fourth job increases aggregate CPU, filesystem, cache, artifact, and network load by one setup copy. There is no repository evidence that four jobs exhaust runner capacity or contend enough to increase user-visible latency; measured PR runs instead show a 54-second reduction in the slowest smoke job.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. The diff intentionally exchanges one bounded parallel setup copy for lower required-check latency, and supplied measurements show the critical path improves. Aggregate resource cost alone, without evidenced contention or throughput degradation, is not a reportable performance regression.

Scenarios.Scenario: Product-affecting PR runs Linux Electron smoke tests when workspace images or dependency caches are cold/unavailable
Scenarios.CriticalPath: All four jobs independently take fallback checkout/install/download paths before running their shard; PR Gate waits for the slowest fallback job. These operations remain parallel rather than serial.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: On misses, restore/download package caches or run apt update/install and pnpm installs.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Four independent miss paths versus three. Each job can retry bounded installs; no per-suite multiplication occurs.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same cold path existed in three shard jobs; the diff adds one concurrent copy.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cold installation is on every shard's critical path; the gate waits for the slowest one.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Restore Electron archives or download and prepare Electron on cache miss.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Four preparations/restores versus three, with up to three download attempts per failing job.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Three shard jobs independently performed the same operation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must complete before each Electron smoke runner starts.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Clone the smoke-test fixture repository with bounded retries.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Four clones, or up to twenty attempts only if all four independently fail repeatedly, versus three clones/up to fifteen attempts before.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Root setup blocks each shard's suites.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: A fixed fourth shard combined with cache/image misses or transient download failures; cost does not scale with the number of suites because setup is once per job.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Up to four concurrent workspace restores/checkouts/package installs/Electron preparations and repository clones, versus three before. Retries are bounded per operation but are not globally limited or coalesced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cold misses amplify the extra job's network and installation work; successful future jobs can use repository-managed caches/images, but running shard jobs do not coalesce an in-flight miss. Failure retries are bounded.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the increase from three to four concurrent cold setup paths; insufficient evidence for a concrete adverse performance outcome.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Cold-path durations and service capacity are not measured in the diff. The mechanism of one additional concurrent miss path is certain, but whether it causes throttling, queueing, or a slower gate is unsupported.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. The concurrency burst is bounded and intentional, and there is no evidence that the extra cold-path request crosses a service or runner limit or outweighs the reduced suite duration.

Scenarios.Scenario: PR does not affect product tests, so Linux Electron smoke jobs are skipped
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Detect Changes sets electron_smoke_affected false; all four smoke job definitions are skipped and linux-tests/PR Gate can progress without executing their shared steps.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: The changed-path classification, not suite count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Zero smoke jobs execute, both before and after the diff.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No workspace, dependency, Electron, or smoke-fixture cache is accessed by skipped smoke jobs.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance change on this path.

Scenarios.Scenario: Linux sharded smoke execution computes suite placement using the new platform-specific duration table
Scenarios.CriticalPath: At smoke-runner startup all suites are registered, selectShardSuites estimates their durations in memory, sorts 33 indexes, and filters the selected subset before Mocha executes the root before hook and suites. The balancing computation is negligible and does not add an external boundary.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: In-memory traversal of Mocha suites, map lookups, sorting, and assignment.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once per shard over about 33 suites: four O(n log n) computations versus three. This is tiny compared with smoke setup and execution.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same algorithm ran once in each of three jobs with a shared duration table and a 20-second default.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs synchronously before tests but has negligible fixed cost at this collection size.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Optional stable-release metadata fetch/download and smoke fixture repository clone after selection.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: In PR CI the runner has no --build, so stable-code download is skipped; each shard clones one fixture repository. In other Linux --build invocations stable setup remains once per shard exactly as before.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical setup boundaries existed; only estimated weights and Linux's default estimate changed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The duration table only changes suite placement; it does not add or move these setup boundaries. Root setup still runs before the selected suites.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of registered top-level suites (about 33) and fixed shard total (four in Linux PR CI).
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Assignment is recomputed once in each of four jobs with identical inputs; suite execution is disjoint by shard index. No new asynchronous concurrency is introduced by the table.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The duration map has no external cache. The smoke fixture is job-local and absent on fresh runners; stable-build download is not reached in the changed PR workflow invocation.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High that the new table changes only assignment and that each suite remains selected once.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Measured suite durations vary by run and first-launch placement, so exact balance can drift, but stale estimates affect only bounded shard balance and not total suite cardinality.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. The changed metadata improves expected balance without introducing expensive work, retention, or boundary fan-out.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed all four changed files and the complete diff inventory under the performance focus. Traced the Linux PR gate, shared workflow setup, cache miss paths, Electron/smoke subprocesses, fixture clone, artifact uploads, and in-memory sharding. The only material cost increase is one bounded parallel copy of per-job setup; the suite set remains deduplicated and measured critical-path latency improves, so no actionable performance regression was found.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
